structure._note: Grades are numbered 1-12 for basic education and T1-T4 for tertiary. 'periods' switch the cycle structure by reference year (UIS convention: the year in which the school year ends).
structure.upper_secondary_note: K-12 (RA 10533, 2013): Grade 11 first offered SY2016/17 (reference year 2017), Grade 12 SY2017/18. Grade-10 completers from reference year 2016 onward go to Grade 11 instead of tertiary.

entry_age._note: Share of children who START Grade 1 at age 6 (rest at 7). WDI official entrance age is 7 to 1997 and 6 from 1998, but actual entry shifted gradually; universal kindergarten (RA 10157, 2012) completed the shift. DECLARED ramp.

costs_share_of_gdppc._note: Annual household cost of a year of schooling (fees, uniforms, transport, materials, plus forgone earnings of the child), as a share of GDP per capita. DECLARED, order-of-magnitude, documented in docs/assumptions.md. Only ratios between sectors/levels and the dated policy changes matter for identification; the overall scale is absorbed by the cost coefficient.

policy_events.what: Free Public Secondary Education Act (RA 6655, 1988): public secondary tuition abolished from SY1988/89.
GASTPE / Education Service Contracting subsidies for private secondary places (RA 6728, 1989).
Senior high school vouchers for public JHS completers enrolling in private SHS (DepEd voucher programme).
Free tuition in state and local universities and colleges (RA 10931, 2017; first applied AY2017/18).

tertiary_public_capacity._note: Public (SUC/LUC) first-year places as a share of the population at tertiary entry age. Rationed; private institutions absorb the rest at private cost. The growth rule is a competing hypothesis (fiscal | responsive | trend), see docs/model.md.

targets._note: Non-WDI observed targets. Each entry names its source.

1985.source: PIDS RA 10931 process evaluation seminar, CHED basic data (private share 79% AY1984-85)

2000.source: UP CIDS HERPRP 2022: private share 68% in 2000

2015.source: UP CIDS HERPRP 2022: private share 48% in 2015
2015.note: CONFLICT: CHED Table 1 gives 54.1% private for AY2015-16 (2,219,857 of 4,104,841). The 48% secondary-source figure is kept but flagged; CHED is preferred where both exist.

2019.source: PIDS RA 10931 process evaluation seminar, CHED basic data (53% AY2018-19); note IPPA paper gives 47% for 2018

income_gradient_2019._note: PIDS DP 2021-42 (Reyes), preliminary APIS 2019 participation, poorest vs richest decile. Age bands and denominators not stated: used only as a directional ratio, never as a level.
income_gradient_2019._moved: Moved from test to calibration on 2026-11-21 (PROTOCOL amendment A3): the only observation that pins the cross-sectional income gradient separately from demand growth over time.

shs_private_share_2019.source: DepEd SY2018-19: senior high total 3,022,841, DepEd public 1,599,637 (52.9%); remainder private, SUC/LUC and overseas

jhs_private_share_2019.source: DepEd SY2018-19: junior high total 8,320,627, DepEd public 6,840,249 (82.2%)

transfers.what: Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) conditional cash transfers to poor households with children in school (pilot 2008, scaled up 2010-2013; institutionalised RA 11310, 2019). Modelled as a cost reduction for the poorest three deciles.

v5._note: Inputs used only by engine5 (PROTOCOL_v5). DECLARED unless a source is given.

direct_costs_share_of_gdppc._note: Out-of-pocket cost per pupil-year as a share of GDP per head, before c_scale (fitted to FIES 2003/2006 education shares). Relative schedule DECLARED from: CHED tuition per unit AY2018-19 (SUC ~PHP 275, private ~PHP 760; ~42 units/yr) against GDP per head; DepEd no-collection policy; FIES composition (fees ~70%, allowance ~17%, supplies/books ~11%).

forgone_earnings_share_of_gdppc._note: DECLARED: forgone child or youth earnings per school year, share of GDP per head. Enters the burden, not spending.

policy_events.what: RA 6655 free public secondary tuition; other costs remain (Bray: fee-free is not cost-free).
ESC/GASTPE subsidies for private secondary places.
SHS voucher (PHP 17,500-22,500 vs GDP per head ~PHP 150k).
RA 10931 free tuition and fees at SUCs/LUCs; living costs, books, transport remain.

driver_map._relational_note: Wage/salary employment proxy. Occupation series are short, classification-break series and are not spliced.
